under-construction.name: Under construction
under-construction.description: Old Oak Common, the interchange being built in west London for HS2, where the Elizabeth line and Great Western trains will also call on new surface platforms; its box was dug by 2024 and it is due to open with HS2's first services in the early 2030s.

surrey-canal.name: Surrey Canal station
surrey-canal.description: An infill station on the Overground between Surrey Quays and Queens Road Peckham, by Millwall's ground, first funded in 2011 as New Bermondsey and renamed Surrey Canal in 2021; it has planning permission but is still awaiting the funding to build it.

bakerloo-extension.name: Bakerloo line extension
bakerloo-extension.description: TfL's extension of the Bakerloo line from Elephant & Castle under the Old Kent Road to New Cross Gate and Lewisham, safeguarded in 2021 and on hold for funding, with a later phase taking over the Hayes line and its Beckenham Junction spur, as consulted in 2014.

crossrail-2.name: Crossrail 2
crossrail-2.description: A second cross-London railway from south-west London and Surrey to the Lea Valley, tunnelled from Wimbledon to Tottenham Hale and New Southgate; its route was safeguarded in 2015 and consulted on that year, with Balham preferred to Tooting Broadway and Wood Green offered instead of Turnpike Lane and Alexandra Palace, before it was shelved in 2020.

dlr-thamesmead.name: DLR to Thamesmead
dlr-thamesmead.description: TfL's branch of the DLR from Gallions Reach to Beckton Riverside and under the Thames to Thamesmead, consulted in 2024 and 2025 and backed by borrowing approved in 2025; construction could start in 2029 for an opening in the early 2030s.

west-london-orbital.name: West London Orbital
west-london-orbital.description: An Overground route from Hendon to Hounslow over the Dudding Hill freight line and the Kew curve, with new stations at Neasden, Harlesden, Old Oak Common Lane and Lionel Road; promoted by TfL, the West London Alliance boroughs and the OPDC, it went to its first public consultation in autumn 2026.

croxley-rail-link.name: Croxley Rail Link
croxley-rail-link.description: The Metropolitan line diverted from Croxley over the disused Croxley Green branch to Watford High Street and Watford Junction, with new stations at Cassiobridge and Watford Vicarage Road; approved in 2013 and begun in 2017, it was halted in 2018 for lack of funding and abandoned.
